title: Loki backend cannot sync rule groups on home cluster (namespace-scheme vs Loki router collision)
description:
Task 24 e2e run (docs/e2e.md §4) found: this operator's namespace scheme
(rulesNamespacePrefix/CR-namespace/CR-name, e.g. e2e/e2e/homelab) always
embeds a literal '/'. On this cluster's Loki 3.6.7, the ruler HTTP
router 404s on any per-namespace/per-group route (GET-single, POST
create/replace, and by the same logic DELETE) once the namespace
contains an embedded '/' -- confirmed independently of the operator
with direct curl, both through the gateway and hitting Loki directly.
Only the bulk GET /loki/api/v1/rules works. Mimir's ruler is
unaffected (same multi-segment namespace shape syncs fine).

Production tenant 1's existing Loki rules already work around this by
using a single-segment namespace (loki-homelab, no embedded '/'),
almost certainly written directly to the ruler's S3 store rather than
through this API.

Consequence: the Loki backend of alerts-operator is non-functional on
this cluster as currently namespaced. Needs a design decision:
(a) a Loki-specific namespace join character that avoids embedded '/'
    when backend: loki (e.g. join with '.' or '-' instead of '/'), or
(b) investigate/upgrade this Loki deployment's ruler routing.
(a) is the lower-risk fix since it's entirely within this project's
control; (b) depends on infra outside this repo.

Full investigation and evidence: docs/e2e.md §4,
.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-21-alerts-operator/task-24-report.md.
notes: Coordinator verified independently against live Loki 3.6.7 on 2026-09-23. POST /loki/api/v1/rules/flatns -> 202; POST /loki/api/v1/rules/e2e%2Fe2e%2Fudm -> 404. Tested five slash-free separators (- _ . : __): ALL give POST=202, per-group GET=200, DELETE=202. This also disproves the project-wide assumption, recorded in CLAUDE.md and the design spec, that Loki 3.6.7's per-group GET is malformed — per-group GET works fine; the slash in the namespace was the sole cause. The bulk-GET-only workaround in internal/backend/loki was therefore built on a misdiagnosis. Blocks a meaningful v0.1.0: every rule namespace the operator creates contains slashes, so no AlertRuleGroup can ever sync to Loki. Note k8s names cannot contain '_' or ':', so either is an unambiguous separator; '-' and '.' are ambiguous because k8s names contain them freely.

comments.author: Marius Antonsen
comments.text: Code fix landed: Loki rule namespaces join on '_' (<prefix>_<ns>_<name>); Mimir keeps '/'. rulesNamespacePrefix pattern tightened to ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$ (forbids '_'), CRDs regenerated. compile gained NamespaceSeparator/BackendNamespace(be,..)/OwnedNamespacePrefix/OwnsNamespace; every call site (compile.Rules, prune ownership, keep map, finalizer, status.backendNamespace) now names its backend explicitly. backend/fake models Loki's decoded-path routing so a slash-containing namespace 404s in unit tests. Malformed-404 misdiagnosis corrected in CLAUDE.md, design spec, docs/migration.md, docs/e2e.md, loki client comments. Unit suite + lint green; 2 Codex rounds (round-1 P1 backend-switch keep-window regression fixed; round-2 P1 rejected on premise, second half documented+tested). STILL OPEN: live-cluster verification never ran - cluster was off (home power outage). Must prove a Loki AlertRuleGroup reaches Synced=True and appears in GET /loki/api/v1/rules, plus before/after prod tenant 1 & anonymous byte sizes. See docs/e2e.md §8 and .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-21-alerts-operator/loki-separator-report.md.

title: ContactPoint Accepted does not run validateReceiver, so one malformed receiver blocks a whole tenant's Alertmanager
description:
Final whole-branch review F3 (.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-21-alerts-operator/final-review.md).

internal/controller/contactpoint_controller.go:56-70 checks only spec.tenantRef and Secret
existence. compile.validateReceiver (internal/compile/validate.go) exists, is per-receiver and is
attributable, but is never run until the Tenant reconciler compiles the whole document.

Contrast AlertRuleGroupReconciler (alertrulegroup_controller.go:73), which runs validateRuleGroups
-> compile.ValidatePromQL at Accepted time, so a bad rule group is excluded from listChildren and
cannot affect anyone else.

Failure: any namespace with RBAC to create a ContactPoint writes
  webhook: [{url: "not-a-url"}]  with tenantRef: homelab
CEL passes (MinLength=1 only), so Accepted=True. The Tenant's compile.Alertmanager then fails at
validateReceiver (compile/alertmanager.go:231) and returns before producing a document, so EVERY
route change, every other team's ContactPoint and the whole routing tree stop reaching
Alertmanager for that tenant. The offending object gets Synced=False/Invalid, but its
Accepted=True is what `kubectl get contactpoints` and the ArgoCD health check
(docs/argocd-health.md) show first.

Amplified by compile.Alertmanager emitting receivers for every ContactPoint referencing the tenant
whether or not the policy routes to it (deliberate, commit 5ffaae5): a ContactPoint in a namespace
the policy can never route to can still take the tenant's alerting down.

Fix: call compile.validateReceiver from the ContactPoint reconciler at Accepted time (it will need
the Secret values, or a variant that validates the shape with placeholder secrets), so the blast
radius is one object -- matching AlertRuleGroup.

Same asymmetry applies to NotificationPolicy: matchers and durations are validated only by the
whole-document amconfig.Load, never at Accepted time.

Explicitly out of scope of the final-fixes round (2026-09-23); filed instead.

title: Peer wedged Terminating keeps a healthy Tenant's prune disabled at Ready=False/Conflict indefinitely
description:
Final whole-branch review, compound noted in the Trace D guard-composition table and the closing
paragraph (.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-21-alerts-operator/final-review.md).

Each half is a known P3; together they take a second, healthy Tenant offline for pruning.

  - conflictingTenant (internal/controller/tenant_rules.go:~211 comment) counts Terminating
    Tenants as claimants deliberately: their namespaces stay live until their own finalizer
    removes them, and the CR disappearing is what clears the conflict.
  - A Tenant whose basic-auth Secret is missing cannot build a backend client, so finalize
    returns an error, the finalizer is never removed and the CR sits Terminating forever.

Compound: a peer wedged Terminating on a missing Secret therefore keeps reporting as a claimant,
which disables the SURVIVING Tenant's rule-namespace prune and holds it at Ready=False/Conflict
indefinitely -- a healthy Tenant degraded by a broken neighbour with no bound on how long.

Cross-references:
  - alerts-operator-29k (survivor is not enqueued when a peer disappears, so even a clean
    resolution waits up to resyncInterval)
  - alerts-operator-ztr (residual TOCTOU in the finalizer ownership tie-break)
  - docs/migration.md Appendix B (recovering a Tenant stuck Terminating) -- the reviewer's
    minimum ask was a cross-reference there.

Note the Alertmanager half of this is now different: since the steady-state AM ownership guard
landed (commit 77efadd), a wedged peer also freezes the survivor's Alertmanager document at
AlertmanagerSynced=False/Conflict, not just its prune. That is the intended trade (never destroy
on an unverified claim) but it widens this compound's blast radius, so it belongs in the same
issue.

Possible directions: exclude a Tenant that has been Terminating beyond some bound from the
claimant set; or surface the wedged peer by name in the survivor's condition message so the
operator is pointed at the actual cause rather than at a collision they did not create.

title: Alertmanager's native pushover_configs receiver has never been exercised live
description:
Task 24's §5 "fire a real alert" live-delivery test (docs/e2e.md,
task-24-report.md) repoints the NotificationPolicy's severity=critical
route at a throwaway echo receiver instead of the real keep/pushover
ContactPoints, to prove Alertmanager actually delivers end to end
without depending on Keep (being retired) or paging the user's real
Pushover account.

That proves the generic webhook path -- Alertmanager firing a real
HTTP POST to a receiver on a route match, and sending a resolved
follow-up -- which is the same mechanism the `keep` ContactPoint uses
(webhook_configs, bearer-token HTTP POST). It does NOT exercise
Alertmanager's native `pushover_configs` receiver type, which is a
distinct code path: its own template rendering and its own outbound
call to Pushover's API, not a webhook at all. Section 3's checks only
confirm the *compiled config document* contains a correct pushover
receiver (fields, credentials present) -- a static check, not a live
one. No run to date, by this operator's e2e process or otherwise, has
ever exercised AM's Pushover send path live.

This is a real, currently-unclosed coverage gap, not an oversight to
immediately fix: there is no sandbox Pushover credential in Infisical,
only the user's real production account, and firing a genuine
notification to it as a side effect of an unattended e2e run is
exactly the outcome task 24 was designed to avoid. That judgement call
was correct and should not be reversed by closing this bead reflexively.
Closing this properly needs either a sandbox/test Pushover account, or
an explicit, attended run where the user is told in advance to expect
and check for a real push notification. Until then, this bead is the
record that Pushover's own delivery mechanism is unverified.

title: purge-dev-crds Codex disposition was verified on macOS stock Make only, which silently ignores .SHELLFLAGS
description:
Task 24 fix round 1: purge-dev-crds's partial-state abort bug (Codex
round-2 P2, "Allow CRD purging from partially installed states") was
fixed in this round (Makefile: kubectl get ... 2>/dev/null || true,
wrapped in a { } group before the pipe to wc -l), and re-verified
against a real .SHELLFLAGS-honouring Make (Homebrew gmake 4.4.1, via
`brew install make`) with a stub kubectl reproducing the "no CRDs
registered" case -- confirmed both the bug (unfixed Makefile aborted
before the delete line under gmake) and the fix (reaches and runs the
delete line) under that real Make.

Recording for the record, not as something still broken: the original
"empirically disproven" disposition in the task-24 report was reached
by testing only against this machine's stock /usr/bin/make (GNU Make
3.81, macOS default), which does not support .SHELLFLAGS at all (added
in GNU Make 4.0, 2013) and silently runs recipe shells without -e
regardless of what the Makefile declares. That made a real bug look
fixed. The class of risk -- "verified on macOS Make only" -- is a
standing gap in how this project's Codex-review dispositions get
tested locally, since neither CI nor a fresh macOS clone would
necessarily use a modern Make unless gmake is explicitly installed and
put first on PATH. Consider: documenting in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
that Makefile-recipe verification must use a .SHELLFLAGS-honouring
Make (gmake, or reproduce the shell semantics directly under bash -ec
and say so), or adding a CI/lint check that catches this class of
drift before it reaches a human's "I tested it" claim.

title: Cross-backend keep entry can set kept spuriously (status only)
description: tenant_controller.go:305-308 asserts a cross-backend keep entry cannot set kept spuriously. It can: tenant_rules.go tests the keep map at :136 before OwnsNamespace at :144, so a Mimir-only Tenant can report MimirRulesSynced=Unknown/Pending because of a keep entry belonging to the other backend spelling. Reproduced by the Loki-separator reviewer. Status-only and self-clearing, never causes a wrong delete, but the comment claiming it cannot happen is wrong. Fix by correcting the comment or swapping the ordering.

title: docs/e2e.md-style multi-file sed | kubectl apply silently drops content without --- separator
description: Passing two filenames to sed and piping into kubectl apply -f - concatenates the two YAML docs with no --- separator, so kubectl merges the two flat mappings into one object (later duplicate keys win) -- one of the two objects silently never gets created. Found in task 24's e2e run applying alertrulegroup-mimir.yaml + alertrulegroup-loki.yaml together (docs/e2e.md originally, an earlier draft, later fixed). Audit any other doc/example that concatenates multiple example YAML files this way and either insert an explicit --- between files or apply them separately.

title: Crash between Alertmanager store.Set and the status patch can strand a config
description: syncAlertmanager writes the Alertmanager document to Mimir, then patches status with alertmanagerConfigHash/alertmanagerConfigAddress as the record that this Tenant owns it. A crash in between leaves the document written but unrecorded. Since Task 20's fix gates finalizer cleanup on that recorded hash, a Tenant deleted while in that state leaves the config behind with no CR describing it. Self-heals on any normal retry, because the next sync re-confirms via store.Get and records the hash. Found by Codex during Task 20 fix round 1 and parked deliberately: closing it needs write-ahead intent in status before the backend call, which is a design change, not a patch.

title: Missing basic-auth Secret wedges a deleting Tenant in Terminating
description: If a Tenant's BasicAuthSecretRef target is gone when the Tenant is deleted, backendOptions cannot resolve credentials, finalize cannot reach the backend, and the retry-forever policy keeps the object Terminating indefinitely. Probe-confirmed by the Task 20 reviewer; recovers as soon as the Secret is restored. The retry-forever policy itself is accepted and correct — this is a new trigger for it that operators will hit by deleting a namespace's Secret before the Tenant. Chart/docs task should cover it: document the recovery (recreate the Secret) and consider ordering guidance so the Secret outlives the Tenant.
close_reason: Documented in docs/migration.md Appendix B: recovering a Tenant stuck Terminating (recovery: recreate the basicAuthSecretRef Secret; ordering: delete Tenant before its auth Secret). Task 22.

title: Residual TOCTOU in finalizer ownership tie-break under simultaneous deletion
description: finalizeOwner()/claimants() read Tenants through an uncached APIReader and pick a deterministic lowest-name winner so exactly one of two colliding Tenants performs cleanup. A narrow window survives: if two already-colliding Tenants are deleted with sub-second overlap, both can observe the other as still present (or both as absent) and either double-clean or skip. Documented by the Task 20 implementer under 'Known accepted residual'. Closing it needs real cross-reconcile coordination (lease or a claim annotation), which was out of Task 20's scope. Impact is bounded: cleanup is idempotent deletes, so a double-clean is harmless; the skip case leaves backend state behind with no CR to retry it.

title: Enqueue peer Tenants when an ownership-key collision clears
description: When two Tenants collide on tenantId+backend+prefix, pruning is disabled on both and each reports RulesSynced=False/Conflict. If the conflicting Tenant is then deleted, or changes its (mutable) backend address, only that Tenant is enqueued — the surviving one stays Conflict with pruning disabled until its next resyncInterval (default 5m). Found by Codex during Task 19 fix round 1 (tenant_rules.go:213-216). Bounded and self-healing, and errs safe: nothing is wrongly deleted, and the arrival direction has no destructive window since a peer CR exists before its namespaces do. Fix: a watch mapper enqueueing affected peers on Tenant change. Needs its own design pass — a naive mapper amplifies every Tenant status write into a fan-out across all Tenants sharing a backend.
notes: Task 20 adds a sibling case: when the finalizer skips cleanup because another Tenant is the deterministic claimant, that claimant is not enqueued either, so it does not learn the conflict cleared until its next resync. Same mechanism, same fix (a peer-enqueue watch mapper) — resolve both together.

title: Recompute Alertmanager auth fingerprint after syncRules (TOCTOU)
description: syncAlertmanager resolves backend credentials, then syncRules runs a full List + POST-per-changed-group + DELETEs against Mimir before the second credential resolution. The window between the two resolutions is seconds, not microseconds, and is widest exactly when the backend is slow or unhealthy. Found by Codex during Task 19, parked by the implementer on a 'microsecond window' argument the task reviewer disproved. Impact is bounded: at most one resync interval of staleness, and a missing secret fails safe. Fix: have authFingerprint take backend.Options (it is Task 19's own new function, so no pinned signature blocks this) and recompute after syncRules.

title: deploy-dev: consider auto-applying refreshed CRDs and a real uninstall guard
description:
Codex review (task 24, round 1 + round 2) flagged two real but
low-severity gaps in the deploy-dev/undeploy-dev Makefile targets,
which were left as-is because their exact content is binding per the
task 24 brief and matches already-documented chart behavior:

1. deploy-dev (Makefile:169-175): helm upgrade skips crds/ once a
   release exists, so a schema/CEL change isn't picked up on redeploy.
   Already documented in the chart's own install NOTES.txt with the
   manual remediation. Consider having deploy-dev apply
   charts/alerts-operator/crds/*.yaml with kubectl apply --server-side
   before the helm upgrade, so this is automatic.
2. undeploy-dev (Makefile:177-178): `helm uninstall ... || true`
   swallows every failure, not just "release not found". Consider
   using helm's own ignore-not-found equivalent instead of a blanket
   `|| true`.
3. Mutable :dev tag + pullPolicy Always won't force a rollout on an
   unchanged pod spec if redeployed at the default DEV_IMG_TAG=dev.
   Already mitigated by recommending a pinned sha tag (which is what
   task 24's actual run used); consider whether deploy-dev should
   force a rollout restart regardless of tag.

None of this blocked task 24's actual e2e run (which used a pinned
sha tag throughout). Low priority polish.

title: purge-dev-crds negative-secret-deletion runbook step: document the ExternalSecret-break technique
description: docs/e2e.md §3's negative test found that kubectl delete secret <name> alone doesn't reliably reproduce SecretNotFound when the secret is owned by an ExternalSecret with creationPolicy: Owner -- ESO recreates it in ~1-2s. The runbook now documents breaking the ExternalSecret's remoteRef.key first to get a stable window. Low priority: just keep this technique in docs/e2e.md if the runbook is re-run; no code change implied.

value: Never wait on a process with pgrep -f "<string>" when the waiting shell's own command line contains <string> — pgrep -f matches full command lines, so the wait loop matches itself and never exits. Cost us 87min: a subagent ran 'until ! pgrep -f "codex exec review"; do sleep 5; done' after launching codex, and four such loops deadlocked. Wait on the PID (wait $!) or match a pattern the loop cannot contain.

In bash, 'set -e' does NOT abort on a negated command: '! grep -q X file' never fails the script, whatever the result. Every 'must not contain X' assertion written that way is silently inert. Found in alerts-operator's chart-test (an injected fake webhook config passed the no-webhook check). Use explicit 'if grep -q X f; then echo FAIL; exit 1; fi' instead. Same trap applies to any '! cmd' and to commands in a pipeline that is not the last element.
